hints: Apply the factor and remainder theorems to translate the two divisibility statements into equations for $a$ and $b$.
Since $2x-1=0$ at $x=\tfrac12$, set $p(\tfrac12)=0$; since $x+1=0$ at $x=-1$, set $p(-1)=12$.
Simplify the two resulting linear equations and solve them simultaneously.
walkthrough:
Apply the Factor Theorem for $(2x - 1)$:
Since $p(x)$ is divisible by $(2x - 1)$, we have $p\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 0$:
$$2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3 + a\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 - 11\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + b = 0$$
$$2\left(\dfrac{1}{8}\right) + \dfrac{a}{4} - \dfrac{11}{2} + b = 0$$
$$\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{a}{4} - \dfrac{22}{4} + b = 0$$
$$\dfrac{a}{4} + b = \dfrac{21}{4} \implies a + 4b = 21$$

Apply the Remainder Theorem for $(x + 1)$:
Since dividing $p(x)$ by $(x + 1)$ leaves remainder $12$, we have $p(-1) = 12$:
$$2(-1)^3 + a(-1)^2 - 11(-1) + b = 12$$
$$-2 + a + 11 + b = 12$$
$$a + b + 9 = 12 \implies a + b = 3$$

Solve the linear system of equations simultaneously:
Subtract $a + b = 3$ from $a + 4b = 21$:
$$3b = 18 \implies b = 6$$
Substitute $b = 6$ into $a + b = 3$:
$$a + 6 = 3 \implies a = -3$$

State the values of the constants:
$$a = -3 \quad \text{and} \quad b = 6$$
